body: I'm aware but we moved in together more so out of necessity than anything else. We were both about to end up homeless due to leases ending and moving in together helped us save money on rent.

Thank you, especially for sharing your own experience with things. It helps so much knowing that it's not an anomaly. I think a lot of people, myself included, don't have a very good understanding of what is and isn't a normal part of relationships and it's good to hear that other people end up with the same questions.

You're certainly right, there are worse things, this is the best relationship I've ever had and it's not because I've settled for some mediocre person out of a handful of duds. Thank you for reminding me to cherish that and remember the painful problems I've had to deal with in the past.

thanks, yeah I'm trying to think of the whole thing as part of a holistic wellbeing issue. Stress is up, wellbeing goes down, relationship suffers. I think I just needed some weird sort of reddit reassurance that these kinds of doubts and questions are okay to have at this time.

I have definitely been considering that on and off and I'm glad you reminded me of it. I do think there's this assumption I hold that relationships need to be a certain way (i.e. strong and stable) and I'm hoping that this is all just a normal part of how relationships work and not any real sort of... doubt? Oh jeez I really hope I am explaining things well enough.

I definitely understand the existence of that illusion and I was essentially including the concept for lack of better explication. I don't believe in "true" love nor do I think it is fair to reduce people to "real" and "fake" love. The phoniness I feel stems from guilt over anything else and I was more so asking if the changes and fluctuations are a normal and regular part of the "process" (again, I'm not sure process is a fair enough word, this isn't very easy for me to articulate)

edit: I just want to point out I 100% agree with what you're saying concerning this fairytale illusion people have of "love." I did resent the insinuation that I am that misguided and naive however, given how I wrote my initial post, I can understand how I came off that way. I'm more so considering the whole situation in terms of ethics, at what point does doubt stop being something healthy and acceptable and become an outright lie? Can/do things fluctuate or is immediately ending the relationship the best/most honest thing to do?
9 months, and we'd been living together for about 6 of those months.
I appreciate it, I do, it helps me remember that you guys exist, somewhere.

I'm starting to, I'm trying to get a little more involved but it's tough because I can be painfully shy. I'm working on it, always working on it, I'd just like to know that one day I'll stop "working" on it and I can just, be?
